notes: Hevel is literally breath or vapor. Its repeated use can suggest transience, frustration, or something that cannot be grasped; one English explanation does not cover every occurrence. “Herding wind” keeps the impossible task pictured by the Hebrew; “chasing wind” is another rendering.

“Things” in verse 8 can also be “words.” The former and later ones in verse 11 may be people or events. Verse 12 begins Qohelet’s first-person royal account; the text’s identification is preserved without adding a personal name.
vocabulary: A Hebrew title related to gathering an assembly, often rendered “Teacher” or “Preacher.” Here the title identifies the book’s questioning speaker.

sections.1: Breath, cycles, and the search for wisdom

notes: The rare expression rendered “concubines in abundance” is uncertain; other kinds of luxury have been proposed. Verse 12’s question about the king’s successor is also compressed and difficult.

Verse 24 is read as “nothing better,” with the comparison supplied by context; it can also emphasize that enjoyment is not in a person’s own control. Verse 25 follows the pinned Hebrew “apart from me.” The alternative “apart from him” changes the speaker’s point and is not substituted silently.
vocabulary: A portion is what the speaker receives to enjoy; gain is the lasting advantage he keeps questioning. The two words are not interchangeable.

sections.18: What will the next person receive?

notes: The poem sets fourteen pairs of times beside one another. It includes killing, hatred, and war without turning each line into a command. The stone images in verse 5 are left unexplained.

“Eternity” can denote long duration or the whole stretch of time. God seeking what is “driven away” may concern the pursued or what has passed away. The final “there” in verse 17 remains difficult; no location is supplied.

Human and animal mortality are stated together. Ruach can mean breath or spirit; verse 19 emphasizes shared breath, while verse 21 asks about their direction after death. The question is retained as a question.
vocabulary: The share a person receives, here the enjoyment of work amid limits on knowing what comes afterward.
